draft.title: The marketing mix
card: The marketing mix is the set of choices a business makes to sell its good or service. It is often called the 4 Ps: product, price, place and promotion.
what is sold, including its features, quality, design and packaging.
what customers pay, and any discounts or deals offered.
where and how customers can buy it, such as in a shop, online or through a stockist. Promotion is how the business tells customers about it, such as ads, social media posts or sales signs.
draft.remember: The 4 Ps are product, price, place and promotion, and a business makes choices about each one.

a.q: Which choice is about place in the marketing mix?
opts: Selling a product through an online store
Giving a product a new look and packaging
Offering a product at half price for a week
Running ads for a product on social media
a.why: Place is about where and how customers can buy, and an online store is one way. Changing packaging is a product choice, while a half price deal is a price choice. Ads are promotion.
a.clue: Think about where the customer goes to buy.

b.q: Ravi owns a bakery in Bendigo. He starts giving out free samples at the local market to get people to try his new sourdough. Which part of the marketing mix is this?
b.why: Free samples tell customers about the bread and encourage them to try it, so this is promotion. It is not price, even though the samples are free, because he is not changing what customers pay for the loaf. The market is where he is giving them out, but the aim is to get the bread noticed, not to change where it is sold.
b.clue: What is the free sample trying to do for the bread?

a.best: Selling a product through an online store
